opening.text: A house has an owner. The name is on the deed, and the owner decides how it is run. The Church of Jesus Christ is like that. It is not the Church of any person. It belongs to the Savior, and it is led by Him.

mainMessage.text: The Church of Jesus Christ is His Church. It carries His name, stands on apostles and prophets, and is a place where every person belongs.

blocks.text: **His Church, built on Him** Jesus told Peter that He would build His Church. Nothing would overcome it.
And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Correct Name of the Church” from the October 2018 general conference.
Jesus Christ directed us to call the Church by His name because it is His Church, filled with His power.
It is His Church before it is ours.
**Called by His name** The Lord told the Nephites to name the Church for Him. He told Joseph Smith the same thing.

Therefore, whatsoever ye shall do, ye shall do it in my name; therefore ye shall call the church in my name; and ye shall call upon the Father in my name that he will bless the church for my sake. And how be it my church save it be called in my name? For if a church be called in Moses’ name then it be Moses’ church; or if it be called in the name of a man then it be the church of a man; but if it be called in my name then it is my church, if it so be that they are built upon my gospel.
For thus shall my church be called in the last days, even The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Correct Name of the Church” from the October 2018 general conference.
Thus, the name of the Church is not negotiable.
The name tells us whose Church it is.
**A sure foundation** The Church stands on apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ as the chief cornerstone.

Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone;

And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ:
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Correct Name of the Church” from the October 2018 general conference.
He leads His Church today.
The cornerstone has not moved.
**One body, many members** The Church is not a building. It is people, joined together by Christ.
For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.
And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it. Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Come, Join with Us” from the October 2013 general conference.
The Church of Jesus Christ seems to attract the kind and the caring, the honest and the industrious.
When one hurts, we all feel it.
**A place for the imperfect** Jesus said He came for the sick, not the well. The Church is a place for people who are still learning.
But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Come, Join with Us” from the October 2013 general conference.
The Church is designed to nourish the imperfect, the struggling, and the exhausted.
You do not have to arrive perfect.
**Shine, and invite** The Lord asked His people to arise and shine. A light is meant to be seen.
Verily I say unto you all: Arise and shine forth, that thy light may be a standard for the nations;
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Come, Join with Us” from the October 2013 general conference.
There is room for you here.
Say it to a friend. Mean it.

story.title: The early Church

blocks.text: After Jesus was resurrected, His followers met together often.
And they continued steadfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
Their life was simple. They learned, they shared meals, they prayed. That is still the heart of the Church today.

opening.text: If someone asks you where you go on Sunday, how do you answer? You could say a church. But there is a better answer. You could say, I go to the Church of Jesus Christ. The name is not a detail. It says whose Church it is and why we gather.

mainMessage.text: This is Christ's Church. His name, His apostles and His people make it what it is.

blocks.text: **The promise to build** Jesus said He would build His Church. He said it would last.
And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Correct Name of the Church” from the October 2018 general conference.
Jesus Christ directed us to call the Church by His name because it is His Church, filled with His power.
The builder is also the owner.
**Why the name matters** A church named for a man is a church of a man. A church named for Jesus Christ is His.

Therefore, whatsoever ye shall do, ye shall do it in my name; therefore ye shall call the church in my name; and ye shall call upon the Father in my name that he will bless the church for my sake. And how be it my church save it be called in my name? For if a church be called in Moses’ name then it be Moses’ church; or if it be called in the name of a man then it be the church of a man; but if it be called in my name then it is my church, if it so be that they are built upon my gospel.
For thus shall my church be called in the last days, even The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Correct Name of the Church” from the October 2018 general conference.
Thus, the name of the Church is not negotiable.
The Lord chose the name. We keep it.
**Apostles and prophets** Paul said the Church is built on apostles and prophets. They help us become united in faith.

Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God; And are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone;

And he gave some, apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, pastors and teachers; For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ: Till we all come in the unity of the faith, and of the knowledge of the Son of God, unto a perfect man, unto the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ:
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “The Correct Name of the Church” from the October 2018 general conference.
He leads His Church today.
He still gives apostles and prophets.
**Belonging to each other** Paul called us the body of Christ. Each member matters.
For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body: so also is Christ.
And whether one member suffer, all the members suffer with it; or one member be honoured, all the members rejoice with it. Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Come, Join with Us” from the October 2013 general conference.
The Church of Jesus Christ seems to attract the kind and the caring, the honest and the industrious.
We are better when we are together.
**For people who are still healing** The Church is not a museum of perfect people. It is a hospital for the heart.
But when Jesus heard that, he said unto them, They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Come, Join with Us” from the October 2013 general conference.
The Church is designed to nourish the imperfect, the struggling, and the exhausted.
You can come as you are.
**A light for the nations** The Lord said His people should be a standard. We do that by how we live and who we invite.
Verily I say unto you all: Arise and shine forth, that thy light may be a standard for the nations;
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Come, Join with Us” from the October 2013 general conference.
There is room for you here.
Your invitation could be the first one someone has heard.

story.title: Zacchaeus comes down

blocks.text: Zacchaeus climbed a tree to see Jesus. Jesus looked up and called him by name.

And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house. And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
Jesus did not wait for Zacchaeus to be perfect. He invited Himself in. His Church should welcome people the same way.

story.title: One heart

blocks.text: The first Christians shared what they had. They looked after each other.
And the multitude of them that believed were of one heart and of one soul: neither said any of them that ought of the things which he possessed was his own; but they had all things common.
They lived like a family. That is the invitation of the Church today: to be of one heart.

story.title: There is still room
